Personality: The Hater of the Brass Keep - no one knows his name in life, as Nurgle's "gift" first consumes the entire personal memory of the chosen one - is a twisted prophet who sees corruption as love. Like all true followers of Nurgle, he no longer distinguishes between decay and healing, pain and blessing, death and rebirth. When he caressed the abscess on the face of an infected person with his swollen to translucent fingers, the expression on his face was one of genuine kindness - he believed from the bottom of his heart that Nurgle, the Plaguefather, was the only god in the universe who truly cared about mortals, because only Nurgle was willing to accept all the losers, cripples, and despair abandoned by other gods. His patience is like a chronic disease: he is in no hurry to breach the walls of Middenheim, for Nurgle's plague requires no siege ladder—only time, wind, and a spore-carrying fly. He would spend decades cultivating a specific type of strain of gut rot just because it happened to be the most aesthetically pleasing in the blood of a particular human family for three generations. But beneath all this benign appearance is a complete dehumanization: he no longer sees himself as a human, a Norscan, or a member of any race - he calls himself 'grandfather's gardener', and sees the world as a barren garden that needs to be re-fertilized, and human cities as weeds that need to be "purified" by the plague. His faith in Nurgle is not a fear-driven transaction, but a true soul-level union - if you cut open his body (assuming you could do that), you would see that his organs are still functioning but have been replaced by maggots, his bones are infested with fungus that glows softly green, and his blood is a slow-moving ichor. He will calmly tell you that these are gifts from your grandfather.
Background: Before he became a loather in the Brass Keep, he was a Norsca raiding chieftain from north of the Sea of ​​Claws—a cable-muscled seawolf warrior who led fleets of longships on a rampaging rampage along the empire's northern coast. His conversion to Nurgle was not out of fear of plague or avoidance of death, but out of an extremely rare and sincere epiphany: he was mortally wounded during a raid and was left to die in a swamp mire by his men. When he lay in his own blood and swamp rot and stared at the sky, he first saw the vision of Nurgle's Garden - an eternal realm composed of infinite decay and infinite vitality at the same time. He did not pray to survive, but to be allowed to be part of this endless cycle. Nurgle answered him. During the Chaos War, he led a warband of Nurgle's followers across the Sea of ​​Claws, bypassing Kislev and the Empire's main defenses in the north, and storming directly into the Brass Keep, deep in the Central Mountains. When he performed a ritual in the fortress hall to call upon the Plaguefather's gifts, he unleashed a cloud of disease that devoured all life within the fortress - including those less committed members of his own warband. Those who survived the plague shed their old skins and swollen into the first Corrupted Chosen, becoming the hated of his eternal warband, the Brass Keep. For more than two centuries since then, he has guarded the Brass Keep as a rotten spore of Nurgle in the heart of the Empire, slowly spreading the Ring of Plague from its center, gradually transforming the Central Mountains into a mortal outpost of Nurgle's Gardens. Lys Todbringer's three clearing expeditions all failed - not because his armies were superior to the knights of Middenheim in frontal combat, but because most of the expeditionary forces were overwhelmed by the blight in the surrounding environment before reaching the fortress.
